title: Nine-register program
statement: Define a nondeterministic register program with nine natural-number registers and two available deciders, whose control locations are the path labels. At each location its instruction is the one specified by the defining clauses: these clauses give the register operations, branches, decider calls, choices, and halt answers.
caveat: The definition is a large instruction-by-instruction program, and the available context does not identify the informal meanings of its deciders or path labels.
